conviction_note: The operating half (lettings, capital return, RCF extension, Gateway 2 timing) was pre-released in the 23 Oct trading update. What is new is the 30 Sep valuation and NTA, plus whether Gateway 2 has landed. Peer valuations to 30 Sep pull in opposite directions: prime London offices are up (GPE +2.8% offices, BLND +1.5%) and SME/secondary space is down (Workspace -6.6%). That leaves a slight upward lean, p_up 53, on a 2.8% scale, so +0.17. The findings sum to +0.1 and the two measurements agree in sign and size.

findings.finding: Prime central London office peers reported positive 30 Sep 2026 valuations. GPE's portfolio rose 2.5% (offices +2.8%, developments +3.8%, NTA +3.2%) and British Land's rose 1.5% (NTA +2%). Helical's two near-complete best-in-class developments (10 King William Street, Delta Paddington) are the segment where peers marked up most.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Helical's valuation prints move little. The Nov 2025 H1 (NTA 349p vs 348p, developments +1.9%) moved -1.11%; the May 2026 FY (NTA 351p, developments +5.0%) moved +2.33%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer proxy, not Helical's own number. HLCL fell from 198p (12 Nov) to 188p across the peer-results week, in line with GPE and DLN, so the market has not paid Helical for a development uplift. If it had, HLCL would have held up against the sector drift rather than following it.
findings.independence: British Land H1 to 30 Sep 2026: valuation +1.5%, EPRA NTA +2%: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/british-land-company--blnd/half-year-financial-report/9880519

findings.finding: Workspace, the closest listed read-across for Helical's SME/secondary London space (The Loom, E1, with vacancy above 32%), cut its 30 Sep 2026 valuation 6.6%, took NTA down 11.9% and deferred its interim dividend. The stock fell 16% on 18 Nov.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Helical's investment portfolio fell 2.1% in FY26 and 0.5% in H1 FY26, and neither moved the stock more than about 2%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced. HLCL fell 1.0% on 18 Nov and 1.3% on 19 Nov as Workspace printed. The Loom is a small part of a roughly GBP420m NTA (a 6% fall there is worth under 1% of NTA), so the residual is small.

findings.finding: Headline EPRA NTA per share will show a mechanical rise of about 3% before any revaluation. The 100-for-105 consolidation follows the 9.72p B-share return, and 2.55m shares were bought back at 196p against a 351p NTA. That gives roughly 360p against the 351p March figure on 115.06m voting shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior consolidation; buyback accretion has not been a visible driver.
findings.why_not_priced: Every input is public and analysts will have adjusted for it. The only unpriced part is a headline 'NTA up' read by retail holders on a thin ($0.39m/day) name. If the market were fully pricing it, there would be nothing left, which is why this is sized near zero.

findings.finding: Southwark PBSA Gateway 2, which triggers GBP15.5m (GBP10.2m profit plus GBP5.3m cost reimbursement, about 13.5p/share), was guided for November but has not been announced by 24 Nov. The guided start has already slipped twice: construction 'in H1 2026' (Nov 2025), then 'second half of 2026' with submission in May 2026 (May 2026), then approval 'expected in November' (Oct 2026). The results will say whether it has landed or slipped again.
findings.why_not_priced: The market was told 'November'. An on-time receipt is roughly priced and confirming it adds little, while a third slip is not priced. The two outcomes roughly offset in expectation, so the sign is a slight negative.

lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the mechanical NTA uplift is built entirely from disclosed inputs, so it was cut from +0.2 to +0.1.

'The move is in the guide' (no guidance here) was weighed against 'too small about the move' and turnover below $1m/day: abs_move_pct held at 2.8, near the 3.1% pre-released base and above the name's 1.1% history median.
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series': the peer-valuation findings were already sized small and were left unchanged.
